Corona is an Italian Eurodance/house music group that was formed in the early 1990s. The group is best known for their hit singles "The Rhythm of the Night," "Baby Baby," and "Try Me Out," which became international dance hits and topped the charts in several countries.

Corona was originally formed by producers Francesco "Checco" Bontempi and Antonio "Alien" Romeo, who wrote and produced the group's music. The lead vocals were performed by singer Olga Souza, who was later replaced by Jenny B. The group's sound was characterized by catchy, upbeat dance melodies and Souza's soulful vocals.

"The Rhythm of the Night" became Corona's biggest hit, reaching number one in several countries and becoming a staple of the early 1990s dance music scene. The group's debut album, also titled "The Rhythm of the Night," was released in 1994 and was a commercial success, selling over 5 million copies worldwide.

Corona continued to release music throughout the 1990s and early 2000s, with varying levels of success. Souza returned to the group in 2005, and they released a new album, "Y Generation," in 2007. However, the group has been relatively inactive in recent years, with no new releases since then.

Despite their relative inactivity, Corona remains a beloved and influential act in the dance music world, and their hits continue to be played in clubs and on the radio around the world.
